answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock collateral that grows with the trust it claims, so creating many fake identities spreads the attacker stake thin instead of multiplying influence. Like shale layers, reputation accrues slowly through verified work and is slashed on fraud, while a public audit trail lets peers trace suspicious bursts of new identities, like a raven spotting carrion, back to one funding source and freeze them before they can vote.
